title: A soft rubber ball skips on water more easily than a hard one

cover.alt: Black-and-white high-speed image of a dark ball flying low over a flat water surface, just before it hits.
cover.credit: Belden et al., Nature Communications 2016 · CC BY 4.0

body: Stones skip best when they are flat and meet the water tilted at just the right angle, so a rigid ball makes a poor skipper. A very soft ball changes shape as it lands: it squashes into a disk, tilted in a way that deflects it back up off the water. In 2016, researchers led by Jesse Belden and Tadd Truscott fired silicone rubber balls at water and found they could skip at impact angles nearly three times larger than predicted for rigid spheres. The softer the ball compared with the push of the water, the more it flattens, which is why softer balls skip more easily.

slides.alt: A dark ball flies in from the left and hits a flat water surface at an angle. It squashes into a flattened disk, slides along, and bounces up and out of view to the right, leaving a large air cavity in the water behind it.
slides.caption: High-speed footage: a soft silicone ball hits the water at an angle, squashes into a disk and bounces back up, leaving a hollow in the water.
slides.credit: Belden, Hurd, Jandron, Bower & Truscott, Nature Communications 2016 · CC BY 4.0 · excerpt

left.label: Hard ball
left.text: It stays round. Rigid spheres are only expected to skip when they hit the water at much shallower angles.

right.label: Soft ball
right.text: It flattens into a well-tilted disk, like a skipping stone, and can skip at angles nearly three times steeper.

slides.heading: How stiff were the balls researchers fired at water in 2016?
slides.note: Shear modulus, a measure of stiffness, of the softest and the rigid ball in the 2016 tests.

slides.heading: Waves inside the ball
slides.text: The flattening isn't instant: the impact sends elastic waves running through the rubber, and how fast they travel decides how the ball's shape changes during the skip. After it leaves the water the ball keeps wobbling, stretching one way and then the other.

slides.question: Why does squashing on impact help a soft ball skip?
slides.explanation: A flat, well-angled disk is the shape that skips best, which is why flat stones work. A soft ball briefly turns itself into one.

source.label: Nature Communications (2016): Elastic spheres can walk on water
